model_annotation:
These two bar plots (labeled (a) and (b)) illustrate the inference time measured for baseline Llama models, distilled Llamba (pure Mamba) models, and MambaInLlama (hybrid) models at the 1B and 3B parameter scales, respectively, across varying batch sizes.

**Plot (a): 1B Models.** The x-axis is labeled "Batch size" and displays categorical values at 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 300. The y-axis is labeled "Inference time (seconds)" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10 seconds. Three bar groups are shown at each batch size: Llama-1B (blue), Llamba-1B (orange), and MambaInLlama-1B (red). At batch size 1, all three models show similar inference times around 1.5–2 seconds, with speedup annotations of ×3.6, ×3.3, and similar values noted. As batch size increases, the Llama-1B bars grow substantially, reaching approximately 10 seconds at batch size 256 and similarly at 300. The Llamba-1B and MambaInLlama-1B bars remain considerably shorter across all batch sizes. Speedup annotations are displayed above the bars, showing values such as ×3.1 at batch size 32, ×2.8 at batch size 64, ×3.7 at batch size 256, and ×3.7 and ×3.2 at batch size 300.

**Plot (b): 3B Models.** The x-axis is labeled "Batch size" with categorical values at 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512. The y-axis is labeled "Inference time (seconds)" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 30 seconds. Three bar groups are shown: Llama-3B (blue), Llamba-4B (orange), and MambaInLlama-3B (red). At batch size 1, all three models show similar inference times around 2–3 seconds, with speedup annotations of ×2.6. As batch size increases, the Llama-3B bars grow substantially, reaching approximately 28 seconds at batch size 256. The Llamba-4B and MambaInLlama-3B bars remain much shorter. Speedup annotations include ×2.6 at batch sizes 16 and 32, ×2.3 at batch size 64, ×2.9 at batch size 128, ×4.7 at batch size 256, and ×4.2 and ×5.1 at batch size 512. Notably, at batch size 512, only the Llamba-4B and MambaInLlama-3B bars appear, suggesting the Llama-3B model could not fit at that batch size.
